children: South Korea plans to sharply reduce its reliance on Middle Eastern crude oil, seeking to diversify import sources and ease vulnerability to geopolitical risks.

Asia's fourth-largest economy, which sourced about 70% of its crude-oil imports from the Middle East in 2025, aims to cut that share to below 50% by 2035, the country's industry ministry said Wednesday.
For natural gas, South Korea aims to keep the share of imports from the Middle East below 30% by 2035, the ministry said.
The ministry noted that conflicts in the Middle East underscore the risks of concentrated energy supply chains, which can threaten industrial activity and livelihoods during a crisis.
The prolonged Iran war has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz, a major global energy shipping route through which 61% of South Korea's oil imports passed in 2025.
The ministry also said that South Korea will expand its crude-oil storage capacity by 20 million barrels by 2030.
